title: SLO-driven traffic splitting playbook (wip)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for running SLO-driven traffic splits (canaries and A/B experiments) across Redwood Console routes. The goal is to provide an operational pattern that balances safety (latency, errors, correctness), statistical validity for product-facing A/Bs, and minimal manual overhead for eng + SRE.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to endpoint-level changes: model variant swaps, quantization profiles, batching/runtime flags, and inference routing policy changes.
- Not a replacement for full product A/B framework for UX experiments (but should interoperate with it).
- Intended for medium-risk to high-risk server-side changes where latency/availability regressions are possible.

Quick summary (1-pager):
1) Define SLOs and guardrail metrics up-front (primary SLOs and emergency guardrails).
2) Select traffic buckets and staging order (canary -> ramp -> full; or A/B 50/50 for product impact experiments).
3) Automate rollout with health checks and rollback triggers; require explicit manual approval at each escalation boundary for non-automated rollouts.
4) Run minimum experiment length with pre-specified statistical tests for A/B.
5) Capture and store detailed telemetry for post-run analysis and automated quality alerts.

Definitions used here:
- Canary: incrementally exposing a small percent of production traffic to a change to validate system-level behavior and key SLOs.
- A/B: randomized experiment to measure customer-facing product metrics; requires independent analysis and usually longer run windows.
- Guardrail: fast-reacting signal used to automatically abort or roll back an ongoing rollout (e.g., p95 latency spike, 5xx increase).
- SLO-driven decision: rollout stage transitions are gate-kept by SLO evaluation windows, not purely calendar time.

SLOs and priority signals (examples):
Primary SLOs (must be defined per-route):
- p50 / p95 latency (in ms) - route SLO: p95 < 250ms
- 5xx error rate - route SLO: < 0.1%
- User-facing accuracy proxy (if available) - model delta within +/- 2% of baseline on key eval set

Fast guardrails (for automatic abort within minutes):
- sudden >50% relative increase in 5xx over baseline in 5m rolling window
- p95 latency increased by >2x relative to baseline sustained for 10m
- Outlier memory/GPU OOMs (any) or queue length spike indicating resource exhaustion

Slow guardrails / analysis signals (for manual review):
- change in per-request token cost >10% sustained over 1h
- model quality regressions on preselected examples or continuous eval set
- error taxonomy shift (new error classes)

Traffic split strategy templates:
- Safety-first canary (recommended for infra/runtime changes): 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%
  - Each stage minimum dwell: 30m (0.5%/2%), 1h (10%), 2h (25%), 4h (50%)
  - SLO checks after each dwell period; abort on any fast guardrail trigger

- Quality-first canary (recommended for model changes with customer-visible output): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%
  - Run paired-eval on sampled requests at each stage; require no regression on held prompts and manual QA signoff at the 20% checkpoint

- A/B experiment (product metric measurement): random 50/50 or weighted (e.g., 70/30)
  - Pre-register hypothesis, primary metric, minimum detectable effect, and sample size calculation before starting
  - Minimum duration often 1 week (business cycles), but can be shorter for high-throughput non-seasonal routes

Automated gating rules (example):
- For each stage, run the following checks using the last X minutes of telemetry (configurable):
  - error_rate_5xx_roll = if current_5xx / baseline_5xx > 1.5 for 5m => abort
  - p95_latency_roll = if current_p95 > 2 * baseline_p95 for 10m => abort
  - infra_signal = any OOM / node_restart => abort immediately
  - token_cost_delta = if avg_token_cost > baseline_cost * 1.1 for 60m => manual_review

Responsibilities matrix (short):
- Product (owner): define primary business metric, hypothesis, rollout risk tolerance, and QA checklist.
- Eng (owner): implement rollout config, smoke tests, instrumentation, and automated rollback hooks.
- SRE: ensure infra observability is present, tune guardrails, and own high-severity incidents and rollback authority for infra-related failures.
- Analytics/Data: register experiment in experiment catalog, run significance tests, and publish analysis.
- Support/CS: prepare playbook snippets for customers and expected FAQs if rollout affects customers.

Pre-launch checklist (must pass before any traffic is sent):
- [ ] Route-level SLOs declared in the Console for this rollout
- [ ] Baseline metrics stored (7d baseline recommended)
- [ ] Health-check probes implemented for new variant (smoke endpoint)
- [ ] Telemetry tags: experiment_id, stage_id, variant_name, allocation_percent
- [ ] Automated guardrail checks enabled in rollout config
- [ ] Runbook + on-call rotation notified with Slack link and escalation path
- [ ] Canary test on staging that mirrors production load (if possible)

Runtime checks and observability requirements:
- Telemetry streams to include per-request metadata: model_id, quantization_profile, runtime_flags, token_count, upstream_latency, downstream_latency, error_class
- Dashboards: real-time 1m and 5m aggregates for p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, GPU utilization, and queue length
- Alerting: separate alert thresholds for rollouts vs. normal production (higher sensitivity during rollouts)
- Traces: sample traces for both baseline and candidate to enable quick diffs in behavior

Experiment analysis guidance (A/B):
- Pre-register: metric, direction, MDE (minimum detectable effect), alpha (0.05), power (0.8), and sample size calculation
- Use stratified sampling if traffic has heavy geo/device skews
- Primary analysis: Wald test or bootstrapped confidence intervals for mean metric; for proportions use chi-square / Fisher exact as appropriate
- Always compute and report: effect size, CI, p-value, and practical significance discussion

Rollback and post-rollout steps:
- Automated rollback should be executed on fast guardrail failure; record time and trigger reason in experiment log
- If manual rollback is performed, create incident note, slot immediate postmortem with stakeholders, and mark experiment as 'failed' in experiment catalog with root cause hypothesis
- For successful rollouts, snapshot config and tag the rollout as a release candidate in the model registry and console

Runbook snippets for on-call (pseudocode):
- abort_if("5xx_spike"):
    if rolling_5m_5xx > baseline_5xx * 1.5:
        set_traffic_allocation(candidate: 0%)
        notify(#rollouts-alerts, message)
- escalate_if("infra_oom"):
    if any_node_oom == true:
        set_traffic_allocation(all: baseline)
        page_sre_team()

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- How to integrate model-quality automatic checks that are tolerant to distribution shift (avoid false positives)?
- Standardized minimal dwell times per traffic tier (data-driven suggestion needed)
- Should token-cost guardrails auto-abort or just surface for manual review? Different customers will want different policies.
- Add runbook template for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where we might not have the same telemetry granularity.

Next steps and owners:
- Jonah: prototype auto-gates in traffic-router and run synthetic canary jobs (ETA 2w)
- Priya: map per-route SLO defaults and add to Console route definition page (ETA 1w)
- Ethan: analytics experiment registration flow changes so experiments are linked to route config (ETA 3w)
- Marta: update rollout-alerting runbook and create Slack shortcuts for abort/rollback (ETA 1w)

References and quick links:
- Experiment index (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ROLL/Traffic+Experiment+Index
- Traffic router service: github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-router
- Experiment catalog: JIRA-RND-814

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and SLO-first. Looking for feedback on: 1) guardrail thresholds and default dwell times, 2) what to automate vs manual, and 3) how to handle low-traffic routes (special casing for sample size).

End of document.
